answer: Resisting sybils means designing for scarcity, not for trust. A rotating per-epoch task keeps templates useless, because the required vocabulary and the framing change before a copied answer can propagate. Think of it as a anchor the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single haven of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a echo of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
